minor: "A week later, the chief executive's memo": 31 January to 8 February is eight days. Saying "Eight days later" or "The next week" would be more exact.

"Quoting a Nokia employee" for the PowerPoint line: the listed source supports the quote and that it concerns Chinese makers. It does not say a Nokia employee said it. Confirm against the memo text or drop the attribution.

"Fifteen months later, Microsoft wrote most of it off": the source gives a 7.6 billion dollar write-down on 8 July 2015, about 14.5 months after closing. 7.6 billion dollars is roughly the 5.44 billion euro price in dollars, so "most of it" is loose. Say "wrote down 7.6 billion dollars", which the sources support.

"In the first quarter of 2012, Samsung passed Nokia... That same month, Standard & Poor's cut...": the quarter ran January to March, while the S&P cut was 27 April and Strategy Analytics reported in April. "That spring" or "The same month the data came out" is safer.
Cold open "Nokia sells its phone business" on 3 September 2013: that was the agreement. The sale closed on 25 April 2014, which the script does say later.
"Nokia's biggest buyers were mobile carriers" has no `sources` entry. It is plausible but unsourced.
"Symbian fell faster than Lumia rose" is an inference from the shipment figures and has no explicit source.
"Eight months" (11 Feb to 26 Oct 2011, about 8.5 months) is a derived figure and is fine.
